rv.q: This intelligent, finely crafted show will probably be best appreciated by the adults in the room, yet there is plenty to intrigue, even delight the youngsters.
Nate Bertone's production is lavish but also pleasingly resourceful.
This is a modern yet timeless version of Alice In Wonderland, where the journey remains enchanting and thoughtful, appealing to both nostalgic adults and wide-eyed children.

There are plenty of inventive touches throughout, such as the oversized teardrops that stream from Charlotte Bradley’s suitably doe-eyed Alice, or when Daniel Page’s Queen of Hearts sings “pink flamingo club” at the start of the croquet match.
A feast for the eyes, it produced audible gasps as well as laughs, which is as good a reason as any to go and see it.
To look at, this production is breathtaking.

cn.t: Critics find this visually lavish production a mostly enchanting treat for young audiences, with Bertone's imaginative design earning wide praise, though some feel the condensed, vignette-style storytelling leaves the magic feeling rushed.
